surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Rantanen forces overtime with just five seconds left, and the Stars win it
paras: Miro Heiskanen was back in the lineup after missing five games. William Karlsson opened the scoring for the Golden Knights just 40 seconds into the second. The third period brought five goals. Karlsson scored his second of the night midway through the period to make it 2-0, but Nils Lundkvist cut Vegas’ lead to 2-1, 32 seconds later. Brett Howden stretched the lead to 3-1 with a little over seven minutes left. With the goalie pulled and a little over a minute left, Wyatt Johnston pulled the Stars within one. With the goalie still pulled and just five seconds left, Mikko Rantanen made it 3-3. Heiskanen won it in overtime. Rantanen finished with four points on a goal and three assists.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jake Oettinger made 24 saves for the Stars, and Adin Hill stopped 18 of 22 at the other end.

Neither power play scored: the Stars killed all five Golden Knights power plays, and the Golden Knights killed both of Dallas’. The Stars improved to 13-6-2 and climbed to second in the Central, while the Knights dropped to 13-6-4, second in the Pacific.
